method: same method as eval/raw/customer_latency_fix_2026-09-21.json: 50 POST /chat calls as Meena (CUST-MEENA), one fresh visitor per call, 15-message pool cycled, local API process (uv run uvicorn services.api.main:app --port 8080), TAAL_MODEL_BACKEND=vertex
substitute_lookup_finding: None of the product-availability / substitute-lookup messages (do you have chips/tea/quinoa/kaju katli/cola, is bread in stock) show a SUSTAINED >7s p50 or p95 on this run: worst p50 is 5.96s ("what tea do you have?"), worst p95 is 11.20s ("do you have quinoa?", driven by one 12.35s outlier out of 4 calls, not a consistent pattern). Per the task instructions, tool-vs-model profiling is only triggered by a consistent >7s pattern, which this run does not show, so no profiling script was written. This does not reproduce yesterdays one-off 7.6s/8.3s figures as a persistent regression -- 2026-09-21s run was 10 calls; this is 50, and only 3/50 calls here exceed 7s, none in the same message twice.
methodology_note: This run followed an earlier, corrupted attempt on the same day: a port-8080 uvicorn process serving this measurement was killed mid-run by an unrelated command targeting that port (an unqualified pkill -f during separate verification work), producing 37/50 real calls and 13/50 connection-error rows in a since-discarded calls.json. That partial file was deleted and this 50/50-clean run replaces it entirely; the port-8080 server was restarted once and left untouched for the remainder of this run. No prompt or model setting was changed in this branch.
